Part two. But inside the building, the secret was ugly. The Edison did not work. It gave wrong results. So, behind closed doors, Theranos ran most blood samples on ordinary machines bought from other companies. Workers who asked questions were watched, threatened, or fired. Two young employees could not stay silent. Erika Cheung, and Tyler Shultz, saw patients getting wrong results. Then a reporter named John Carreyrou, at the Wall Street Journal, got a tip and started digging. He published anyway. October 2015. The article hit like a bomb. Walgreens ended the partnership. Two years of test results were thrown out. Forbes changed her fortune from four and a half billion dollars, to zero. In January 2022, a jury found her guilty of defrauding investors. She was sentenced to more than eleven years in federal prison. The girl who wanted to be a billionaire got her wish. Then she lost it all. Subscribe to Rise and Ruin for more.
